name: Genetic Difference of Sex Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Statement on Management of Intersex Disorders

criteria.description: Presence of ambiguous or atypical external genitalia at birth
Discordance between chromosomal sex and gonadal sex identified by karyotyping and gonadal biopsy or imaging
Abnormal serum hormone levels indicating atypical sex steroid synthesis or action
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex development pathways

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia or discordant chromosomal and gonadal sex plus supportive hormonal or genetic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and urology.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes atypical phallus size, labioscrotal fusion anomalies

searchTerms: mismatch between chromosomes and physical sex
high blood pressure from adrenal enlargement
hypertension due to adrenal gland problem
blood pressure raised by adrenal hyperplasia

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric distress related to gender identity

laboratory: Abnormal serum sex steroid hormone levels (e.g., testosterone, estradiol, 17-hydroxyprogesterone)
Electrolyte imbalances in congenital adrenal hyperplasia
imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing presence or absence of Müllerian structures
MRI or ultrasound of gonads to detect dysgenesis or tumors
genetic: Karyotype analysis revealing sex chromosome anomalies (e.g., 46,XY; 46,XX; mosaicism)
Molecular genetic testing identifying mutations in SRY, SOX9, NR5A1, AR, CYP21A2 and other sex development genes
other: Psychosocial assessment for gender identity and support needs

distinguishingFeatures: Normal to elevated testosterone with androgen receptor mutations

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Salt-wasting crisis or adrenal insufficiency symptoms
Rapid onset of virilization or feminization during infancy or puberty
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Pediatrics. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Global Disorders of Sex Development Update since 2006. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
Orphanet: Genetic difference of sex development (ORPHA:325690)
